description: This bar chart illustrates the average change using compression for two conditions, “Inferred Frames” and “Lexical Signal”, across different observation probabilities. The horizontal axis represents “Observation Probability” with categories labeled 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9, appearing in ascending order. The vertical axis is labeled “Average Change Using Compression” and represents a linear scale ranging from -3 to 2, with tick marks at intervals of 1. For each observation probability, there are two adjacent bars representing the average change for each condition. The “Inferred Frames” condition is represented by gray bars, while the “Lexical Signal” condition is represented by light yellow bars. At an observation probability of 0.2, the “Inferred Frames” bar extends to approximately 0.4, while the “Lexical Signal” bar extends to approximately 0.8. At an observation probability of 0.9, the “Inferred Frames” bar extends to approximately -1.2, and the “Lexical Signal” bar extends to approximately 1.8. No bars are visually emphasized, and the chart does not appear to be sorted in any particular order beyond the ascending order of observation probabilities on the horizontal axis.
